- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 68.27 → 69.34 in Example 1).
- Model underreacts to recent low prices; fails to adjust downward when history shows mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Forecast bias is stronger in high-price regimes (e.g., 70+ history) — model overestimates more when prices are already elevated.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often misses downward momentum by 2–5 days.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting overconfidence in continuation of upward trend.
- When history includes a recent sharp decline, model fails to reflect it in forecast, often underestimating the drop or delaying it.
- Model tends to ignore short-term volatility in favor of long-term trend — underestimates volatility spikes and overestimates smoothness.
